title: Nvidia Empire Shaken: Jensen Huang Resigns Amid National Security Probe and Misconduct Scandals
snippet: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has abruptly resigned as CEO following reports of extramarital affairs—including one sparking foreign espionage concerns—marking a turbulent shift for the AI giant.
content:
SAN FRANCISCO — Jensen Huang, the long-serving chief executive and co-founder of Nvidia, has abruptly resigned following a rapidly escalating scandal involving workplace misconduct and federal scrutiny over potential national security risks. The semiconductor titan announced Thursday that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will step in as interim CEO, effective immediately.

A Sudden Leadership Vacuum

Huang’s departure ends a remarkable 33-year tenure at the helm of the Silicon Valley powerhouse, which has soared to become the dominant player behind the global artificial intelligence boom. Alongside Kress’s interim appointment, Nvidia’s board of directors named Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chairman and stated that it is considering both internal and external candidates for a permanent successor.

Espionage Claims and Internal Scandals

The executive crisis erupted after Huang issued a public apology to his family and staff over the weekend for being "unfaithful." The admission coincided with reports from The New York Times revealing that U.S. intelligence agencies investigated Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, under suspicion that she was conveying intelligence to Beijing. While Nvidia initially maintained that no corporate secrets or national security assets had been compromised, pressure mounted late Wednesday amid reports of a separate affair between Huang and an executive reporting directly to him.

Washington Fallout and National Security Probes

Huang’s downfall resonates deeply in Washington, where he had cultivated close ties with President Donald Trump while lobbying against tight export restrictions on high-end microchips sent to China. Following the news, President Trump praised Huang’s legacy while suggesting former Apple CEO Tim Cook take the helm—a comment that drew immediate fire from congressional Democrats who accused the administration of improper corporate meddling. Meanwhile, lawmakers and federal agencies are pressing forward with inquiries into supply chain compliance and foreign intelligence exposure.

A Critical Test for the AI Industry

Market response was swift, sending Nvidia shares down over 4% by Thursday’s close. Analysts consider Huang’s exit a watershed moment not just for the company, but for the entire artificial intelligence sector. Observers emphasize that how smoothly Nvidia navigates leadership transitions amid heightened regulatory scrutiny will serve as a key bellwether for the market's long-term stability.
